extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants and practitioners (attorneys/agents) and USPTO examiners preparing or evaluating patent application drawings for U.S. applications
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and requirements for preparation, content, form, submission, correction, and acceptance of drawings and photographs in U.S. patent (utility, design, plant, reissue) applications under 37 CFR 1.84 and related MPEP sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use PTOL-90 or PTO-90C as cover sheet
rubrics_metrics.description: Use a PTOL-90 or PTO-90C form as a cover sheet for this communication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant should also amend the specification to refer to the new illustration at the time of submission of the drawing(s). This may obviate further correspondence where an amendment places the application in condition for allowance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptable drawing categories
rubrics_metrics.description: There are two acceptable categories for presenting drawings in utility and design patent applications: (1) Black and white; (2) Color (including color photographs/drawings) under specified conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Black and white drawings are normally required; color drawings/photographs have special requirements and, for utility applications, generally require a petition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Photographs ordinarily not permitted — exceptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Photographs, including photocopies, are not ordinarily permitted in utility and design patent applications but will be accepted if photographs are the only practicable medium for illustrating the claimed invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples where photographs/photomicrographs are acceptable: electrophoresis gels, blots, autoradiographs, cell cultures, histological tissue cross sections, animals, plants, in vivo imaging, thin layer chromatography plates, crystalline/metallurgical microstructures, textile fabrics, grain structures, and ornamental effects in design patents. If subject matter admits illustration by drawing, examiner may require a drawing in place of the photograph. Photographs must be of sufficient quality so all details are reproducible in the printed patent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Color drawings/photographs — petition and requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Color drawings are permitted in design applications; color drawings/photographs in utility applications are accepted only after a granted petition under 37 CFR 1.84(a)(2) or (b)(2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petition must include: the fee (§ 1.17(h)); one set of color drawings if submitted electronically or three sets if paper; and an amendment inserting a specified paragraph in the brief description of drawings stating the file contains color drawings and copies will be provided upon request and fee. Color drawings/photographs must be of sufficient quality that all details are reproducible in black and white. Petitions are decided by a Supervisory Patent Examiner and may be renewed for continuing applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification of drawings
rubrics_metrics.description: Identifying indicia should be provided on drawing sheets and, if provided, should include the title of the invention, inventor’s name, and application number or docket number.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If provided, this information must be placed on the front of each sheet within the top margin. Each drawing sheet submitted after the filing date must be identified as either 'Replacement Sheet' or 'New Sheet' pursuant to § 1.121(d). Marked-up copies of amended drawing figures including annotations must be clearly labeled 'Annotated Sheet' pursuant to § 1.121(d)(1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Graphic forms in drawings
rubrics_metrics.description: Chemical/mathematical formulae, tables, and waveforms may be submitted as drawings and are subject to the same requirements as drawings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each chemical or mathematical formula must be labeled as a separate figure (using brackets when necessary). Each group of waveforms must be presented as a single figure with a common vertical axis and time along the horizontal axis; each individual waveform discussed in the specification must be identified with a separate letter designation adjacent to the vertical axis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Type of paper
rubrics_metrics.description: Drawings must be made on paper which is flexible, strong, white, smooth, non-shiny, and durable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All sheets must be reasonably free from cracks, creases, and folds. Only one side of the sheet may be used. Sheets must be reasonably free from erasures and free from alterations, overwritings, and interlineations. Photographs must be developed on paper meeting sheet-size and margin requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Size of paper
rubrics_metrics.description: All drawing sheets in an application must be the same size; acceptable sizes are: (1) 21.0 cm by 29.7 cm (DIN A4), or (2) 21.6 cm by 27.9 cm (8 1/2 by 11 inches).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It is required that all drawing sheets in a particular application be the same size for ease of handling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Margins and sight area
rubrics_metrics.description: Sheets must not contain frames around the sight and should have scan target points printed on two cater-corner margins. Minimum margins: top 2.5 cm (1 inch), left 2.5 cm, right 1.5 cm (5/8 inch), bottom 1.0 cm (3/8 inch).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These margins leave a sight no greater than specified dimensions depending on sheet size; frames around sight are not permitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Views required and placement
rubrics_metrics.description: Drawings must contain as many views as necessary to show the invention (plan, elevation, section, perspective, detail views). All views must be grouped together and arranged on the sheet(s) without wasting space, preferably upright, clearly separated, and not included on specification/claims/abstract sheets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Views must not be connected by projection lines and must not contain center lines. Waveforms may be connected by dashed lines to show relative timing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exploded views
rubrics_metrics.description: Exploded views with separated parts embraced by a bracket are permissible to show relationships or order of assembly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When an exploded view is on the same sheet as another figure, the exploded view should be placed in brackets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Partial views
rubrics_metrics.description: Large machines/devices may be broken into partial views on a single sheet or extended over several sheets if no loss in facility of understanding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Partial views on separate sheets must be capable of being linked edge to edge so no partial view contains parts of another partial view. Include a smaller scale view showing the whole and indicating positions of parts. Enlarged portions must be separately labeled as distinct views.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multi-sheet single complete view
rubrics_metrics.description: Where views on two or more sheets form a single complete view, the sheets must be arranged so the complete figure can be assembled without concealing any part of any view on the various sheets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Very long views
rubrics_metrics.description: A very long view may be divided into several parts placed one above the other on a single sheet.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The relationship between the different parts must be clear and unambiguous.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sectional view conventions and hatching
rubrics_metrics.description: Sectional view planes should be indicated on the view from which the section is cut by a broken line, with ends designated by numerals corresponding to the sectional view number and arrows indicating direction of sight.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hatching must indicate section portions by regularly spaced oblique parallel lines spaced to be distinguished; should not impede reference characters and lead lines. Hatching preferred at ~45°. If reference characters must be inside hatched area, break off hatching where characters are inserted. Cross sections must show all materials and hatchings should accurately indicate material nature; juxtaposed different elements should have different hatch angles; large areas may confine hatching to an edging. Different hatching types have conventional meanings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternate position depiction
rubrics_metrics.description: A moved position may be shown by a broken line superimposed upon a suitable view if this can be done without crowding; otherwise a separate view must be used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Modified forms shown separately
rubrics_metrics.description: Modified forms of construction must be shown in separate views.

rubrics_metrics.name: Arrangement of views orientation
rubrics_metrics.description: One view must not be placed upon another or within the outline of another; all views on the same sheet should stand in the same direction and, if possible, be readable with the sheet upright.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If views wider than sheet width are necessary, the sheet may be turned so the top is on the right-hand side. Words must appear left-to-right horizontally when upright or turned, except for graphs using standard axis convention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Front page view selection
rubrics_metrics.description: One of the views should be suitable for inclusion on the front page of the patent application publication and patent as the illustration of the invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant may suggest a single view (by figure number) for inclusion. Views must not be connected by projection lines and must not contain center lines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scale requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Scale must be large enough to show the mechanism without crowding when the drawing is reduced in size to two-thirds in reproduction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indications such as 'actual size' or 'scale 1/2' are not permitted since they lose meaning with reproduction in different formats.

rubrics_metrics.name: Character of lines, numbers, and letters
rubrics_metrics.description: All drawings must be made by a process giving satisfactory reproduction: every line, number, and letter must be durable, clean, black (except color drawings), sufficiently dense and dark, uniformly thick and well-defined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Weight of lines and letters must be heavy enough to permit adequate reproduction; applies to fine lines, shading, and cut-surface lines. Different line weights may be used where they have different meanings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Shading conventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Shading is encouraged if it aids understanding and does not reduce legibility; used to indicate surface or shape of spherical, cylindrical, and conical elements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Spaced thin lines preferred; shading lines must contrast with rest of drawing. As substitute, heavy lines on the shade side can be used if they do not obscure reference characters. Light should preferably come from the upper left at 45°. Solid black shading areas are not permitted except for bar graphs or representing color.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of graphical symbols
rubrics_metrics.description: Graphical drawing symbols may be used for conventional elements when appropriate; elements using symbols must be adequately identified in the specification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ANSI and ISO symbol publications are considered generally acceptable as guides but the Office will not approve a collection as a group; symbol clarity decided case-by-case. Avoid overly specific or unclear symbols; in design patents use judiciously as they may interfere with showing appearance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legends
rubrics_metrics.description: Suitable descriptive legends may be used subject to approval by the Office, or may be required by the examiner where necessary for understanding of the drawing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Legends should contain as few words as possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference characters rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Reference characters (numerals preferred), sheet numbers, and view numbers must be plain and legible and must not be used with brackets or enclosed outlines; they must be oriented in same direction as the view.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: English alphabet must be used for letters except where another alphabet is customarily used. Reference characters must measure at least .32 cm (1/8 inch) in height, not cross or mingle with lines, not be placed on hatched/shaded surfaces (unless underlined and space left in hatching). The same part appearing in more than one view must always be designated by the same reference character; the same character must never designate different parts. Reference characters not mentioned in the description shall not appear in the drawings; reference characters mentioned in description must appear in drawings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lead line rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Lead lines (lines between reference characters and details) may be straight or curved and should be as short as possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: They must originate in the immediate proximity of the reference character and extend to the feature indicated. Lead lines must not cross each other. Lead lines are required for each reference character except for those indicating the surface or cross section on which they are placed; such reference characters must be underlined. Lead lines must be executed like other lines in the drawing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Arrows usage
rubrics_metrics.description: Arrows may be used at the ends of lines provided their meaning is clear.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specified uses include: (1) freestanding arrow on a lead line to indicate an entire section towards which it points; (2) arrow touching a line to indicate the surface shown by the line looking along arrow direction; (3) to show direction of movement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copyright or mask work notice placement
rubrics_metrics.description: A copyright or mask work notice may appear in the drawing but must be placed within the sight immediately below the figure representing the copyrighted/mask work material and be limited to letters .32 to .64 cm high.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Content of notice must be limited to elements provided by law (e.g., '©1983 John Doe'); inclusion permitted only if authorization language in § 1.71(e) is included at the beginning of the specification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Numbering of sheets
rubrics_metrics.description: Sheets of drawings should be numbered in consecutive Arabic numerals starting with 1 within the sight.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Numbers must be placed in the middle of the top of the sheet (not in the margin) or on the right-hand side if drawing extends close to the top center. Sheet numbering must be clear and larger than reference characters. Show number as 'sheet_number/total_sheets' using two Arabic numerals separated by an oblique line.

rubrics_metrics.name: Numbering of views
rubrics_metrics.description: Different views must be numbered in consecutive Arabic numerals starting with 1, independent of sheet numbering and, if possible, in the order they appear on the drawing sheet(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Partial views intended to form one complete view must be identified by the same number followed by a capital letter. View numbers must be preceded by 'FIG.' Where only a single view is used, it must not be numbered and 'FIG.' must not appear. Numbers identifying views must be simple, clear, and larger than reference characters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Security markings location
rubrics_metrics.description: Authorized security markings may be placed on the drawings provided they are outside the sight.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preferably center security markings in the top margin.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corrections must be durable and replacement sheet procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: Any corrections on drawings submitted to the Office must be durable and permanent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Corrections to drawings must be made in the form of replacement sheets labeled in the header 'Replacement Sheet' since the Office does not release drawings for correction. If a marked-up copy of any amended drawing figure, including annotations indicating the changes made, is filed, such marked-up copy must be clearly labeled as 'Annotated Sheet.' See 37 CFR 1.121(d) and MPEP § 714 for amendment of drawings procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: No holes in drawing sheets
rubrics_metrics.description: No holes should be made by applicant in the drawing sheets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of drawings and references
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific rules apply for design drawings (§ 1.152), international design reproductions (§ 1.1026), plant drawings (§ 1.165), and reissue drawings (§ 1.173(a)(2)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See referenced MPEP sections for details. Good quality copies acceptable if lines uniformly thick, black, and solid.

rubrics_metrics.name: Facsimile transmission restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: Black and white drawings are permitted to be transmitted by facsimile if submitted after the filing date; color drawings are not permitted by facsimile.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should ensure the facsimile process does not unreasonably degrade drawing quality. See 37 CFR 1.6(d)(4).

rubrics_metrics.name: Certified copies for noncompliant application-as-filed drawings
rubrics_metrics.description: For certified copies of an application-as-filed which does not meet sheet size/margin and quality requirements of 37 CFR 1.52, 1.84(f), and 1.84(g), see MPEP § 608.01.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions for drawing status
rubrics_metrics.description: Definitions: Original drawings (submitted with application at filing); Substitute drawing (filed later than filing date usually to replace unacceptable original); Acceptable drawing (acceptable for publication/issuance); Corrected drawing (includes corrections of informalities/changes approved by examiner); Unacceptable drawing (drawings not complying with 37 CFR 1.84).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Drawings that do not comply with form requirements may still be acceptable for purposes of publication and examination if readable and reproducible; Office will object only when unable to reproduce the drawing or contents unacceptable to the examiner.

rubrics_metrics.name: India ink (black ink) requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: India ink, or its equivalent that secures solid black lines, must be used for drawings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Black and white drawings are normally required in utility patent applications. See MPEP § 608.02(c) for information relating to location of drawings in IFW applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Black and white photographs submission rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Black and white photographs may be accepted in lieu of India ink drawings only for inventions incapable of accurate depiction by India ink drawings and must comply with 37 CFR 1.84(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No petition or petition fee required for B&W photographs; only one set is required. Photographs must show the invention more clearly than ink drawings and be of sufficient quality so all details are reproducible. If several photographs are used to make one sheet of drawings, the photographs must be contained on a single sheet.

rubrics_metrics.name: Color drawings/photographs storage and issuance practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Color drawings/photographs will be stored in a content management system and a black and white copy will be placed in the file wrapper along with a placeholder sheet. Utility patents granted on or after April 18, 2023 (egrant) will include color drawings/photographs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Copies of patents with color drawings will be provided by the Office upon request and payment of the necessary fee. Until a petition is granted, examiner must object to color drawings/photographs as improper and require cancellation or substitutes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Renewal of color petition in continuing applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Where color drawings/photographs are filed in a continuing utility application, applicant must renew the petition under 37 CFR 1.84(a)(2) and (b)(2) even if a similar petition was filed in the prior application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Until the renewed petition is granted, the examiner must object to color drawings or color photographs.

rubrics_metrics.name: OPAP review and Notice to File Corrected Application Papers
rubrics_metrics.description: OPAP will review drawings in utility and plant applications for compliance with certain requirements of 37 CFR 1.84 and will send a Notice to File Corrected Application Papers if drawings are unacceptable for publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notice gives applicant two months from mailing date to file acceptable drawings; this period is extendable under 37 CFR 1.136(a). OPAP will not release applications to Technology Centers until acceptable drawings are filed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner action when drawings impede examination or raise 35 U.S.C. 112 issues
rubrics_metrics.description: If at initial assignment or when application is taken up, supervisory examiner believes drawings do not permit reasonable examination, applicant should be required to immediately submit corrected drawings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If drawings permit reasonable examination but are of such character as to render the application defective under 35 U.S.C. 112, examination should begin immediately with a requirement for corrected drawings and a rejection of the claims as not in compliance with 35 U.S.C. 112(a) being made.
